Select strains to sequence, with or without a maximum number of strains

Source: R/select_strains.R
select_strains.Rd

Selects the strains to sequence with the clustering method or with the profile method, taking into account the maximum number of strains that can be sequenced.

Usage

select_strains(
  prepared_data,
  n_max = NULL,
  method = c("clustering", "profile"),
  fill = TRUE,
  weights = NULL,
  k_max = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

prepared_data

A data frame with one row per strain, as returned by prepare_input().

n_max

Maximum number of strains that can be sequenced, or NULL (default) to select the optimal number of strains (one per optimal cluster or one per distinct profile).

method

"clustering" (default) or "profile".

fill

If TRUE (default) and n_max is larger than the optimal number of strains, the selection is completed up to n_max strains with supplementary strains. If FALSE, the selection stops at the optimum.

weights

Clustering method only: numeric vector of weights, one per column of prepared_data (see assess_gower()), or NULL for equal weights.

k_max

Clustering method only: largest number of clusters tested to find the optimum. By default, the number of distinct profiles (beyond it, clusters only split identical strains), limited to the number of strains minus 1. Lower it to save time on large datasets.

seed

An integer passed to set.seed() to make the random choices reproducible (ex aequo strains or groups), or NULL (default).

Value

An object of class strainselect_selection, a list with:

table

prepared_data with the columns cluster (cluster in the final cut of the tree, or group of identical strains numbered by decreasing size for the profile method), optimal_group (cluster at the optimal number of clusters, or group of identical strains), selected (TRUE/FALSE), status ("optimal", "supplementary", "selected" or "not selected"), representative (identifier of the selected strain of the same cluster or group, NA if none) and group_represented (whether the optimal group of the strain contains a selected strain);

selected

identifiers of the selected strains;

method

the method used;

k_opt

optimal number of strains: optimal number of clusters, or number of distinct profiles for the profile method;

k

number of selected strains;

n_max, fill

the arguments used;

silhouette

clustering method: data frame of the average silhouette width (avg_silwidth) for each number of clusters k tested;

groups

profile method: data frame with, for each group of identical strains, its size, its number of selected strains (n_selected) and its profile;

unrepresented_groups

optimal groups without any selected strain (only when n_max is smaller than the optimum);

n_strains, n_profiles

number of strains and of distinct profiles;

weights

the weights of the metadata (clustering method);

gower

the output of assess_gower() (clustering method).

The object has print() and plot() methods, and can be exported with export_selection() or summarised in a report with report_selection().

Details

Clustering method (method = "clustering", default): computes the Gower distances and the hierarchical clustering tree, finds the optimal number of clusters (largest average silhouette width) and selects in each cluster the strain with the largest silhouette width.

Profile method (method = "profile"): groups the strains with identical metadata (distinct profiles) and sorts the groups by decreasing size (ties in random order). One strain per group gives the "optimal" selection. With a smaller n_max, one strain is selected in each of the n_max largest groups. With a larger n_max, supplementary strains are added turn by turn: a second strain in each group that has one, from the largest group to the smallest, then a third strain, and so on. Strains of a group have the same metadata, so the strain(s) of a group are chosen at random.

See also

Other clustering method: assess_gower(), cstats_table(), export_selection(), report_selection(), select_silhouette()

Other profile method: define_profiles(), prepare_upset(), select_profiles()

Examples

prepared_data <- prepare_input(
  salmonella_strains,
  col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
  id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT"
)
#> no duplicate ID
#> selected metadata: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT, ANNEE
# clustering method, no budget: optimal number of strains
res <- select_strains(prepared_data, seed = 1)
res
#> Strain selection (clustering method)
#>   strains: 100 - distinct profiles: 61 
#>   optimal number of clusters (k_opt): 61 
#>   maximum number of strains (n_max): not given
#>   selected strains: 61 (optimal: 61) 
plot(res)

# budget smaller than the optimum
res_20 <- select_strains(prepared_data, n_max = 20, seed = 1)
res_20
#> Strain selection (clustering method)
#>   strains: 100 - distinct profiles: 61 
#>   optimal number of clusters (k_opt): 61 
#>   maximum number of strains (n_max): 20 
#>   selected strains: 20 (selected: 20) 
#>   optimal groups not represented: 41 out of 61 
head(res_20$table[, c("cluster", "optimal_group", "selected", "status")])
#>               cluster optimal_group selected       status
#> 2020LSAL00151       1             1    FALSE not selected
#> 2020LSAL00152       1             1    FALSE not selected
#> 2020LSAL00163       2             2    FALSE not selected
#> 2020LSAL00167       2             3    FALSE not selected
#> 2020LSAL00176       3             4    FALSE not selected
#> 2020LSAL00177       3             5     TRUE     selected
# profile method, budget larger than the number of distinct profiles
res_profile <- select_strains(prepared_data, n_max = 75, method = "profile", seed = 1)
res_profile
#> Strain selection (profile method)
#>   strains: 100 - distinct profiles: 61 
#>   groups of identical strains: 61 
#>   maximum number of strains (n_max): 75 
#>   selected strains: 75 (optimal: 61, supplementary: 14) 
plot(res_profile)

head(res_profile$groups)
#>   group size n_selected
#> 1     1   10          2
#> 2     2    7          2
#> 3     3    5          2
#> 4     4    4          2
#> 5     5    3          2
#> 6     6    3          2
#>                                                                                                                                                    profile
#> 1                                                             Alerte Produit | Viande de dinde | Pays de la Loire | Alimentation humaine | Abattage | 2020
#> 2                     Alerte Produit | Bovins | Auvergne Rhone Alpes | Santé et production animales | Lieu d'exploitation, d'élevage, ou de culture | 2020
#> 3                                          Surveillance | Viande de dinde | Nouvelle Aquitaine | Alimentation humaine | Transformation industrielle | 2020
#> 4                                   Surveillance | Viande porcine | Provence Alpes Cote d Azur | Alimentation humaine | Transformation industrielle | 2020
#> 5 Programmes de contrôle et d'éradication | Gallus gallus | Bretagne | Santé et production animales | Lieu d'exploitation, d'élevage, ou de culture | 2020
#> 6                                                            Surveillance | Viande de canard | Nouvelle Aquitaine | Alimentation humaine | Abattage | 2020
# profile method, budget smaller than the number of distinct profiles:
# one strain in each of the 20 largest groups
res_profile_20 <- select_strains(prepared_data, n_max = 20, method = "profile", seed = 1)
plot(res_profile_20)
